sources.citation: CIESAS Repositorio Institucional (jspui simple-search), Dialnet, CrossRef API, archive.org advancedsearch, Semantic Scholar API, OpenAlex API, Google Books API — queries for Yucuná / Zahuatlán / Amatitlán Mixtec.
sources.note: No linguistic work on this variety found: CIESAS hits are other Mixtec varieties (Alcozauca, Yucuquimi, Ocotepec, Abasolo del Valle); Dialnet and CrossRef return only a socioeconomic article on San Simón Zahuatlán (Martínez Domínguez 2025, Convergencia 32(1), doi 10.29101/crcs.v32i1.24864; Ramales Osorio et al. 2019, RCCS 8).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 (Hammarström et al.). Languoid nort2986 'Northwest Oaxaca Mixtec' and dialect sans1274 'San Simón Zahuatlán'; reference search (langdoc) for titles containing Yucuná / Zahuatlán / Amatitlán / Portezuelo / 'mixteco del noroeste'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No descriptive references for nort2986 (only Josserand 1983, Egland et al. 1983, Auderset et al. 2023); title searches return zero hits for this variety (the 42 'Yucun' hits are Arawakan Yucuna or Yucunany Mixtepec Mixtec). Glottolog places San Simón Zahuatlán under Silacayoapan Mixtec (sila1250), not nort2986.

sources.citation: Auderset, Sandra, Simon J. Greenhill, Christian T. DiCanio & Eric W. Campbell. 2023. Subgrouping in a 'dialect continuum': A Bayesian phylogenetic analysis of the Mixtecan language family. Journal of Language Evolution 8(1): 33-63, plus Supplementary Material 2 'Coding details' (Zenodo 7940497) and lexibank CLDF language table.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress statement for this variety (only remarks on Diuxi and Peñoles tone notation). SM2 Table 1 lists the three mxa towns among Josserand's 1977-78 survey points: amat11 San Miguel Amatitlán, guad11 Guadalupe Villahermosa (El Portesuelo)/Guadalupe Portezuelo, zahu11 San Simón Zahuatlán [sans1274]; Table 4 shows Josserand's Amatitlán wordlist ('amat') has 0% tone-marked entries. The CLDF language table assigns no variety to nort2986 (Zahuatlán is filed under Glottolog dialect sans1274 of Silacayoapan Mixtec sila1250).

sources.citation: INALI. 2008. Catálogo de las lenguas indígenas nacionales: Variantes lingüísticas de México con sus autodenominaciones y referencias geoestadísticas. Diario Oficial de la Federación, 14 Jan 2008.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Entry <mixteco del noroeste> tu'un savi [tũʔũ saβi] covers San Miguel Amatitlán, San Simón Zahuatlán and Santos Reyes Yucuná (incl. 'Guadalupe Villahermosa (El Portesuelo)'); establishes that Ethnologue mxa = INALI 'mixteco del noroeste' (p. 2, Tercera Sección; lines 8979-8984).

sources.citation: Gordon, Raymond G. Jr. (ed.). 2005. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 15th ed. Dallas: SIL International. Entry 'Mixtec, Northwest Oaxaca' [mxa].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Establishes identity: 'Northwest Oaxaca, towns of Santos Reyes Yucuná, Guadalupe Portezuelo, and San Simón Zahuatlán'; 2,500 speakers (1990 census); 'SVO; short words, clitics; tonal.' No bibliography listed. (16th ed. 2009 and 17th ed. 2014 copies also saved; 17th ed. gives 5,430 speakers (2000 INALI).)

sources.note: Only primary data on this variety: 1977-78 survey wordlists from San Miguel Amatitlán, Guadalupe Portezuelo and San Simón Zahuatlán (per Auderset et al. 2023 SM2 Table 1); its Proto-Mixtec chapter is the standard pan-Mixtec statement of stress on the first syllable of the bimoraic couplet, which could be cited second-hand for this variety.
